overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that adding a team_id check to skip conditions would deny teamless keys, but overlooked that UserAPIKeyAuth objects default team_id to None even when a team exists, requiring explicit team_id assignment in the test fixture.
why_it_breaks: The test creates a UserAPIKeyAuth without explicitly setting team_id, so it defaults to None. The production code now checks `valid_token.team_id is not None` before skipping model checks. However, in production, keys created with models=['all-team-models'] may have had team_id implicitly set or handled differently during key generation, meaning they would pass the team_id check and skip model validation. The test fixture doesn't match the production scenario where these keys were working before, causing the fix to break legitimate teamless keys that were intentionally created with all-team-models to grant broad access.

evidence.quote: Both now require `valid_token.team_id is not None` to skip the check. Teamless keys fall through to `can_key_call_model`, which via `_resolve_key_models_for_auth_check` correctly treats the unresolvable sentinel as a non-matching string and denies access
